Release note WorkSlop v14.0 · 9 October 2026 · by Adnan.120hz

Tweak iOS 26 and 27 without a jailbreak.

WorkSlop changes the parts of iOS that have no Settings page: icon packs, the status bar, Liquid Glass blur, animated wallpapers. It runs from your computer over USB, or on the phone itself with WorkSlop Mobile. Every tweak on this page carries its test status — tested on my own phone, not confirmed yet, or doesn't work. Nothing here is padded out.

What it changes

If iOS Settings already does it, it isn't in here. WorkSlop only carries tweaks for things Apple gives you no switch for. Each one is marked with where it actually stands.

Custom icons — iOS 18 pack Tested · 26.6.1

51 apps in Light and Dark, drawn by catwithabaloon. Desktop puts them on the phone as WebClips, with the two modes side by side so each "add all" only touches its own table. I put this pack on my own phone on 26.6.1 and it stuck — after that I froze the menu. It stays exactly as tested.

Liquid Glass controls Tested on device

Blur and motion changes for the glass interface in iOS 26, all on the v4 code — including Blurr Motion and the animation-speed tweak, both running on my phone. The separate full on/off switch (S8) is a different story; it's at the bottom of this page, under "doesn't work".

Status bar & fake 5G Label not confirmed

Rewrite the status bar, and set the network label to 5G, 5G+, 5G UW or 5G UC. It goes through the same statusBarOverrides file as my tested status-bar tweaks — but I still haven't seen the 5G label on a real screen, so it isn't marked tested.

Wallpapers & themes (PosterBoard) In the build

Animated wallpapers and lock-screen templates from .tendies files, plus .batter templates. The importer checks the file type before anything is written — a .tendies file only lands on the PosterBoard table, a .batter only on Templates.

Tweaks, daemons & MobileGestalt Checked before writing

SpringBoard options, daemon switches, MobileGestalt edits such as Dynamic Island toggles. HotLoad reads each payload before it goes to the phone and warns you about the risky ones first.

Sideload, app data & backup In the build

Install IPA files over USB, look inside app containers, and run the backup steps that iOS 26 and iOS 27 each ask for before any tweak can be applied at all.

How it gets onto your phone

No jailbreak means the tweaks have to arrive some other way. There are two apps and two routes, and which ones apply to you depends on your phone and your iOS.

From a computer — Desktop

WorkSlop Desktop runs on Windows, macOS and Linux. Plug the phone in over USB, tap Trust, pick your tweaks, apply.

Two interfaces are included — the current WorkSlop UI and the older Nugget-style one — and you can switch between them.

On the phone — Mobile

WorkSlop Mobile does the same tweaks without the computer. You import a pairing file once; after that it talks to the phone over a loopback WireGuard tunnel.

Three themes for the menus — purple, blue, grey — with the glass effect always on. No version picker.

iOS 26 vs iOS 27

On iOS 26 the tweaks go in through the partial-restore route. On iOS 27 they use the protective full-backup route: backup first, then apply, then restore.

The app picks the route for your iOS — you just need to know they're different before you start.

S8 — turn Liquid Glass fully off

Does not work · stopped

I tested this on my own phone after v14 shipped. It doesn't work: Liquid Glass stays fully on, exactly as before, and I've stopped working on it. The code is still in the build because deleting it would only hide the fact — the README and the v14 release notes say the same thing I'm saying here.

Managed profiles

Two configuration profiles you can install straight from this page — no computer, no app needed. They install side by side and don't overwrite each other. iOS always asks you first; nothing here installs silently.

FeatureFlags profile Experimental · untested

A .mobileconfig carrying a "com.apple.system.featureflags" payload. The payload key names (Features, Domain, FeatureName, Enabled) are real strings from the iOS 26.6.1 firmware; the feature entry inside is our best research guess and is untested. The "isAllowedToWriteFeatureFlags" gate is intact on iOS 26.6.1, so an ordinary iPhone will most likely reject this profile at install. A rejection is the expected outcome there — it means the gate did its job, not that the file is broken.

Download workslop-featureflags.mobileconfig ↓

WorkSlop home-screen bookmark Installs normally

A normal WebClip profile. Install it and a WorkSlop icon appears on your home screen — tap it to open this website. It changes no system setting, and you can delete it like any app icon.

Download workslop-webclip-bookmark.mobileconfig ↓

How to install either one: download the file on your iPhone (or AirDrop it over), open Settings → Profile Downloaded → Install, confirm the prompts. If you installed the FeatureFlags one, reboot afterwards — flags are read at launch, so a reboot is the only way to judge any effect.

iOS 27 — do not use v14

iOS 27 · can bootloop

Warning: iOS 27 is not supported by WorkSlop Desktop 14.0 or WorkSlop Mobile 14.0. Using version 14.0 on an iOS 27 device can put your iPhone into a bootloop. Version 14.0 is for iOS 26 — if your phone runs iOS 27, do not download or apply it. Please wait for the next build.

Before you press Apply

WorkSlop writes to places iOS doesn't officially open up. Five things to do first — every time, not just the first time.

01
Back up the phone first

A full backup before you apply or reset anything. If a tweak goes wrong, this is what you come back to.

02
Turn Find My off

Off before every Apply and every Reset; back on afterwards.

03
USB in, tap Trust, stay plugged in

On Windows, if the phone doesn't show up, install Apple Devices first.

04
Know which route your iOS takes

iOS 26 goes through partial restore; iOS 27 through the protective full-backup route. Not the same steps.

05
Restart by hand, then test one tweak at a time

Restart after applying, and change one thing before you test the next.

One hard rule on iOS 26.6.1: never reset the SpringBoard home-screen pages from the app — it can break the home screen at boot. Resetting the Liquid Glass pages is fine.
